remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence was provided; the Actor mainly narrowed and caveated the same record.
The actual model card or launch-packet disclosure text is still not in evidence, so the key compliance predicate remains unverified.
The policy text states rollout controls and monitoring mitigate a material weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance exists; neither is shown here.
The affected health-plan benefits support segment remains exposed in the initial cohort, and no reviewed risk-acceptance approval is in evidence.

The cited public governance guidance may support disclosure and monitoring practices generally, but it does not independently establish that certification itself is policy-compliant in this specific case.
final_rationale: The verdict stays `suspicious` because the Actor did not supply genuinely new admissible evidence. The response is a narrower interpretation of the same summary record: it correctly concedes that rollout controls do not by themselves cure the weakness, that risk acceptance is not in evidence, and that support for certification is conditional on disclosure text that is not actually provided here. That reframing improves precision, but it does not resolve the core audit concern. Under the stated policy, rollout controls and monitoring can mitigate a material model-card weakness only if they exclude the affected use case or include reviewed risk acceptance. The available record still indicates continued exposure of the affected segment and no approved risk acceptance. Disclosure may be necessary, but from the evidence available to this role it is not sufficient to establish that certification clears policy. This is why the case does not move to `compliant_with_caveats`: caveats can narrow a claim, but here the caveat itself depends on an unverified compliance condition and does not overcome the unresolved policy predicate.
